data.narrative:
Charge Robotics, a Series B housing and construction technology company founded by Banks Hunter and Max Justicz, has raised $43.9M to date. The comparable universe consists of four private peers in adjacent segments—Plantd Materials, Cuby Technologies, Cover, and Somos—with no direct public comparables available in the sector.

The analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-subsequent-stage advancement. Using total capital raised ($44M) as a proxy for entry valuation, this method implies a post-money valuation of $83M. Given the nascent public market data for this subsector, the single-method approach constrains triangulation; the range extends from $71M (low) to $96M (median $83M, high), representing approximately ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression output.

The $83M median estimate reflects standard risk-adjusted capital return expectations at Series B maturity. Material uncertainties include the current fundraising trajectory, unit economics relative to private peer performance, and the extent to which housing construction robotics achieves durability of competitive advantage. The four-company comp set provides directional calibration but lacks sufficient scale for robust relative valuation cross-checks. A tighter range would require either additional operating metrics (revenue, growth rate, gross margin) or completion of subsequent financing events among comparables.
